run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T11:05:05Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by 504 responses on the proxy's own 'ingress' spans (961.29 error spans against 16,215.84 non-error/unset ingress spans over 2026-11-15T10:05:05Z-11:21:25Z). Sampled traces show these are 15-second upstream timeouts: the frontend-proxy 'ingress' span ends with http.status_code=504 and its child 'router frontend egress' span ends error=true, http.status_code=0 after 15,000,766 us, while the corresponding frontend request also lasted ~15 s. The hung requests are cart requests: sampled failing traces are load-generator user_add_to_cart and user_view_cart, and cart's own spans POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem hang for 476-479 s and then fail with otel.status_description "Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis" from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected(); frontend /api/cart returns 500 with the same FAILED_PRECONDITION message and checkout's error spans are on oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder. Cart logs show "Connection failed. Disposing the object" at 11:03:07 and "Wasn't able to connect to redis" repeatedly from 11:05:24 onward. The dependency behind that is valkey-cart: the otel-collector's redis receiver, whose endpoint is configured as valkey-cart:6379, stopped receiving fresh redis values at 11:03:30 (memory/cpu metrics freeze) while the collector itself kept running normally, i.e. valkey-cart stopped answering clients around 11:03. valkey-cart's container stayed Running with 0 restarts and no visible resource saturation (about 0.002 CPU cores against a 10m limit, 3.8 MB working set against a 10Mi limit, 2-6% of CFS periods throttled, memory failcnt 0), so the reason it stopped responding is not visible in the available telemetry (its container emitted no log lines). Node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae is Ready without memory/disk/PID pressure and other pods on it behaved normally, so a node-level failure is not supported.

claims.text: frontend-proxy error spans in the window are confined to its 'ingress' operation: 961.29 error spans for span_name='ingress' versus 16,215.84 non-error (STATUS_CODE_UNSET) ingress spans; no error spans appear on its 'router frontend egress' series in the aggregate by status_code.

Sampled frontend-proxy error traces show 'ingress' spans with status_tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" lasting 15,000,011-15,000,896 us, each with a child 'router frontend egress' span that ends error="true", http.status_code="0" after 15,000,139-15,000,766 us; the matching frontend POST/GET spans in the same traces also lasted about 15 s while recording http.status_code="200".

In the sampled failing traces the requests timing out at the proxy are cart operations: load-generator spans 'user_add_to_cart' and 'user_view_cart' return http.status_code 504, and the corresponding frontend spans are POST /api/cart and GET /api/cart returning http.status_code 500 with exception message "9 FAILED_PRECONDITION: Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis".

cart's own error spans, POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart and POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, carry otel.status_description "Status(StatusCode=\"FailedPrecondition\", Detail=\"Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected() ... at cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.GetCartAsync(String userId)\"" and had durations of 476,482,345-479,682,021 us.

cart container cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logs "Connection failed. Disposing the object" at 2026-11-15T11:03:07.940Z and then "Wasn't able to connect to redis" repeatedly from 2026-11-15T11:05:24Z through 2026-11-15T11:11:41Z (135 matching lines in total in that range).

cart request completions collapse at the same time: for span_name 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart', STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans ran 232-302.7 per 120 s until the window ending 11:04:00 and were 0 in every later window, while STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans appear from the window ending 11:06:00 (5.3-8.0 per 120 s).

frontend-proxy ingress error spans were near zero before 11:06 and then surge: 0 in the 120 s windows ending 11:00-11:04, then about 130.7-146.6 per 120 s from the window ending 11:06:00 through 11:14:00; on 300 s windows the counts are 53.3 (11:00-11:05), 436.7 (11:05-11:10) and 334.8 (11:10-11:15). A much smaller blip of the same span existed at 10:48-10:56 (1.3-2.7 per 120 s).
The otel-collector ConfigMap configures the redis receiver with 'endpoint: valkey-cart:6379', so the redis_* series describe valkey-cart.

Redis telemetry from that receiver stopped changing around 11:03: redis_memory_used_bytes last changes at 11:03:30 (1,710,360) and then holds the identical value at every 30 s step through 11:12:00; redis_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="sys"} stops rising and reads 1.704472 at 11:05:05, 11:07:05, 11:09:05 and 11:11:05; redis_memory_peak_bytes likewise freezes at 1,726,344 from 11:05:05 onward.
The collector itself kept running and being scraped during that period: rate(otelcol_process_cpu_seconds_total) stayed non-zero at every 300 s step from 10:45:05 through 11:15:05 (0.021-0.042 cores).

valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is Running and reports ready with restartCount 0 and start time 2026-11-15T10:31:53Z; its deployment valkey-cart has 1/1 available and ready replicas and defines no readiness probe, CPU limit 10m and memory limit 10Mi (requests 2m/4Mi), image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine.

valkey-cart's container shows no CPU or memory saturation: container_cpu_usage_seconds_total rate was 0.0010-0.0035 cores, the CFS throttled-period ratio was 0.022-0.061, container_memory_working_set_bytes was 3.60-3.98 MB against a 10Mi limit, and container_memory_failcnt stayed 0 through 11:15:05.

valkey-cart is addressable: service valkey-cart is ClusterIP 100.68.233.28 on port 6379 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and its endpoints object contains address 100.96.2.228 targetRef Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr.

cart's container CPU throttling ratio rose from 0.1657-0.2461 in windows before 11:05:05 to 0.8285 (window ending 11:10:05) and 0.8562 (window ending 11:15:05); a whole-namespace filter for ratios above 0.5 after 11:05:05 returned only cart-755465879b-t9mf7 and postgresql-c7fd45b87-2d46r.

Node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, which hosts both cart-755465879b-t9mf7 and valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, reports Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False and PIDPressure=False, and 4 allocatable CPUs / ~16 GB allocatable memory.

Other services also carry error spans tied to the same dependency: checkout has error spans on oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (6.75) and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (6.75), and frontend has error spans on GET /api/cart (31.53), POST /api/cart (46.31), executing api route (pages) /api/cart (79.34), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem (46.31), grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (31.53) and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (7.12) in the window.

The small error counts on ad (2.04), fraud-detection (2.04) and recommendation (3.05) are on flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream or /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans, not on cart operations, and no returned evidence links them to the cart/valkey failure.

A change occurred in the window before the failure: every otel-demo pod carries a start time of 2026-11-15T10:31:53Z-10:33:39Z, cart's current pod comes from ReplicaSet cart-755465879b owned by Deployment cart with image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, and events at 11:07:54-11:07:55Z record '"Killing" Stopping container cart' and 'FailedKillPod ... KillContainerError: rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded' on a previous cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s.

Primary cause: valkey-cart stopped serving clients at about 11:03: cart's first redis connection failure is logged at 11:03:07, the collector's redis receiver (endpoint valkey-cart:6379) stops receiving fresh values at 11:03:30 while the collector itself stays healthy, cart then blocks for 476-499 s per request and returns FAILED_PRECONDITION 'Wasn't able to connect to redis', frontend /api/cart hangs past the proxy's 15 s limit, and frontend-proxy emits the 504 ingress error spans that drive the alert. This is correlation of three independent observations on the same dependency, not a verified internal failure mode of valkey.

Secondary candidate: cart's container is CPU-limited (45m limit) and its CFS throttled-period ratio reached 0.83-0.86 after 11:05:05, which may have amplified how long cart requests hung and how long its redis reconnect attempts took. It is not supported as the initiating cause because the first redis connection failure (11:03:07) and the freeze of the collector's redis data (11:03:30) precede the throttling jump, and redis data collection does not depend on the cart pod.

Node-level failure on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae as the cause is not supported: the node is Ready with no memory, disk or PID pressure, and other pods on it (for example product-catalog) served requests normally (product-catalog spans in the sampled traces completed in 96-143 us) during the incident.

A fault inside frontend-proxy itself is not supported: its non-error ingress spans completed in 2.8-3.7 ms, its 9 error ingress spans are 15 s spans whose child 'router frontend egress' spans ended with http.status_code=0 at the same 15 s, i.e. the proxy was waiting on the frontend and the frontend was waiting on cart.

Valkey resource saturation is not supported as the cause: against its 10m CPU and 10Mi memory limits the container used about 0.002-0.0035 cores, 3.6-4.0 MB working set, was throttled in only 2.2-6.1% of CFS periods and recorded memory failcnt 0; the pod also had 0 restarts, i.e. it was not OOM-killed. The extremely low limits remain a design risk but are not demonstrated to have caused the outage.

Treat valkey-cart as the failing dependency: verify its health directly (retrieve its container logs, since the log stream returned no lines, and inspect the process for blocking/defunct state), and add a real readiness probe to the valkey-cart deployment so that 'ready' reflects a successful PING rather than only a running container.

Raise valkey-cart's CPU and memory limits (currently 10m and 10Mi) so that the datastore has headroom for snapshots and for load bursts, and review cart's 45m CPU limit, whose container reached 0.83-0.86 CFS throttled ratio during the incident.

gaps: valkey-cart emitted no log lines in the authorized window (the log read returned status no_data), so the internal reason it stopped answering (blocking command, fork/save problem, disk/volume issue, kernel D-state, maxclients) cannot be verified from logs.

The RequestErrorRate rule itself could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules for rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data, so the alert's exact expression and label set are unverified; only the underlying frontend-proxy error spans were confirmed.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what triggered the 10:31:53Z-10:33:39Z recreation of all otel-demo pods, and whether anything changed on valkey-cart around 11:03, cannot be verified. The causal link between that rollout and the 11:03 valkey failure is unknown.

The networkpolicy listing for namespace otel-demo returned no data (no policies returned), so the absence of a network policy that could have blocked cart/collector traffic to valkey-cart:6379 is not established.

Prometheus data for the redis_* series ends at 11:11:05 and other series at 11:15:05, and Jaeger span data ends at about 11:12:36; whether valkey-cart recovered after that, or is still unresponsive, is unknown.

The FailedKillPod/Killing events on the previous cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (11:07:54-11:07:55Z) could not be tied to the cart/valkey failure; its node, prior state and whether its termination hang shares a cause with the incident are unknown.

Valkey client-side details (connected clients, maxclients, blocked clients, slowlog) are not exported by the available redis receiver metrics, so the failure mode on the valkey side cannot be narrowed further.
next_steps: Retrieve valkey-cart pod logs from the node (kubectl logs / node container log files) and run INFO, CLIENT LIST, SLOWLOG GET and PING against valkey-cart:6379 to establish whether it is responsive now and what blocked it at about 11:03.
Check node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae kernel/container-runtime logs around 11:03-11:08 (dmesg, containerd logs) for D-state processes, OOM or cgroup errors affecting the valkey-cart container.

Add readiness (PING) and liveness probes to the valkey-cart deployment and raise its 10m CPU / 10Mi memory limits, then re-check cart's 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' rate and the frontend-proxy 504 rate.
Obtain the RequestErrorRate alerting rule from Alertmanager/Prometheus rule files to confirm the expression and the exact metric that reported 1.0888 for otel-demo/frontend-proxy.
